Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Consumer Goods Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.  

Alex Rivera:  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Consumer Goods' Q3 results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and David Kim, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Apex Consumer Goods delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.  

Our discussion today will cover overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, sustainability initiatives, and outlook for the remainder of the year.  

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.  

Michael Chen:  
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $3.1 billion, representing a 5% increase compared to the prior year, with organic sales growth of 4.2%. Gross margin was 48.7%, driven by pricing discipline, favorable product mix, and supply chain productivity. Operating income was $650 million. Diluted earnings per share were $1.25. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.  

I'll now turn to our gross margin performance, which continues to reflect the strength of our CPG portfolio and the effectiveness of our multi-year margin expansion initiatives. For the third quarter, gross margin expanded to 48.7%, up 150 basis points year-over-year and 60 basis points sequentially from Q2. This marks the sixth consecutive quarter of gross margin expansion, bringing our trailing 12-month gross margin to a record 48.2%—our highest level since we divested the low-margin private label business in 2021.  

Let me break down the key drivers behind this outperformance, starting with the positives, which more than offset lingering headwinds.  

First, pricing discipline contributed approximately 320 basis points of expansion. Amid persistent inflation, we implemented targeted price increases averaging 7-9% across our North American portfolio, particularly in high-velocity categories like salty snacks and non-alcoholic beverages. For instance, our CrunchTime snack brand saw a 10% list price hike on premium flavored chips, which we supported with compelling innovation like the new air-fried, plant-based lines that resonated with health-conscious Gen Z consumers. In EMEA, where inflation remains elevated at 5-6%, we captured an 8% pricing benefit on PureGlow personal care products, leveraging our strong household penetration—over 25% share in UK drugstores—to maintain velocity without sacrificing share.  

Second, favorable product mix added 110 basis points. We're accelerating premiumization, shifting 12% of our North America sales mix toward higher-margin segments like organic and functional products. Zest Energy's new zero-sugar, electrolyte-infused RTD beverages, launched in July, delivered 55% gross margins versus our portfolio average, driving a 15% category growth. Globally, this mix shift mirrors trends at peers like Monster Beverage in energy drinks and Clorox in household cleaners, where premium adjacencies are insulating margins from commodity volatility.  

Third, supply chain productivity generated 180 basis points of tailwinds. Our Vitality Operating System—our proprietary ERP and AI-driven platform rolled out across 15 plants last year—delivered $45 million in COGS savings this quarter through predictive demand forecasting and waste reduction. In salty snacks, we've cut french fry yield losses by 18% via automated sorting tech, akin to Frito-Lay's precision agriculture investments. Additionally, our strategic sourcing team locked in fixed-price contracts for 70% of our palm oil needs at Q1 levels, mitigating the 25% spot price surge driven by Indonesian export restrictions. Sustainability initiatives, like regenerative cocoa farming partnerships in Côte d'Ivoire, not only de-risked our $200 million annual cocoa exposure but yielded a 5% cost premium rebate from suppliers.  

On the offset side, commodity inflation pressured margins by 140 basis points, primarily from cocoa (+45% YoY due to West African weather disruptions, echoing Hershey's headwinds) and dairy (+12% on U.S. milk powder tightness). Freight and logistics added a 50 basis point drag, with ocean rates up 20% on Asia-U.S. lanes amid Red Sea disruptions—though our nearshoring of beverage production to Mexico has already offset 30% of this.  

Regionally, the story varies but remains constructive: North America (65% of sales): Gross margin hit 51.2%, up 200 bps YoY, fueled by pricing and mix in snacks and beverages. We're gaining share versus Kellogg and General Mills in cereals-adjacent categories. EMEA (20% of sales): 46.5% margin, flat YoY but with 100 bps sequential improvement. UK and German inflation allowed pricing wins, but energy surcharges on manufacturing lingered. APAC/LatAm (15% of sales): 44.8% margin, up 120 bps, benefiting from yuan devaluation tailwinds on exports and local sourcing in Brazil for personal care actives.  

FX was a modest 20 basis point headwind from a stronger USD impacting our Eurozone revenues.  

Looking forward, we expect Q4 gross margin of 49.0-49.5%, implying another 100-150 bps YoY expansion. This guidance embeds $60 million in additional productivity from our next-gen automation pilots—robotic depalletizers in three U.S. facilities—and continued premium mix growth to 15% of sales. Strategically, we're prioritizing three levers: (1) portfolio pruning of sub-40% margin SKUs, targeting $100 million in low performers like legacy sugary cereals; (2) scaling direct-to-consumer channels via DTC e-comm, where margins exceed 60%; and (3) advancing our net-zero supply chain by 2030, which includes blockchain-tracked sustainable palm oil to capture green premiums from retailers like Walmart and Tesco.  

In summary, our gross margin trajectory underscores Apex Consumer Goods' resilience in a volatile CPG landscape—outpacing peers like Procter & Gamble and Unilever—and positions us to deliver 200+ bps of cumulative expansion by fiscal 2025.  

As we review our Q3 results, I'd like to dive deeper into our market share performance, which continues to outperform the broader CPG category averages per Nielsen and IRI data. Overall, we gained 110 basis points of market share year-over-year across our core portfolio, driven by a combination of volume-led growth in high-margin premium segments and targeted share recovery in staple categories amid persistent inflation pressures. Our All-Commodity Volume (ACV) penetration now stands at 92% globally, up from 89% a year ago, reflecting strong velocity on shelf and expanded distribution through both traditional trade and e-commerce channels.  

Let me break this down by key category, with regional nuances, and highlight the strategic levers we're pulling to sustain this momentum.  

Beauty & Personal Care (BPC) – 45% of Revenue. In BPC, we're up 180 bps YoY to 14.2% market share globally, outpacing category growth of just 1.2%. Premiumization is the tailwind here: our "Radiance Renew" skincare line, positioned against market leaders like L'Oréal's La Roche-Posay and Estée Lauder, captured 2.3 points of share in the $50+ prestige segment, fueled by clean beauty formulations with 95% naturally derived ingredients. In North America, which represents 55% of our BPC sales, we gained 250 bps to 16.8% share, thanks to a 15% uplift in e-commerce ACV via Amazon and Ulta partnerships—our site now ranks in the top 5 for facial serums by units sold. Europe saw modest gains of 90 bps to 12.5%, despite softer demand in value shampoos; however, we're countering this with our "EcoShield" sustainable packaging initiative, which boosted Numeric Distribution (NPS) by 8 points in Germany and the UK. Challenges persist in Asia-Pacific, where we're flat at 9.7% share due to intense competition from local players like Shiseido; that said, our recent JV with a top Indonesian distributor is ramping, adding 400 SKUs and projecting 150 bps uplift in Q4.  

Home Care – 30% of Revenue. Home Care delivered a standout 220 bps gain to 11.9% global share, well ahead of the flat category. Laundry detergents were the hero, with our "PowerClean Pro" pods—now with 30% more cleaning enzymes—stealing 3.1 points from P&G's Tide Pods in the super-concentrate space. Regionally, Latin America shone brightest: up 310 bps to 13.4% share, driven by affordable multipacks that resonated amid 25%+ inflation in Brazil and Mexico; our trade spend efficiency here improved ROI to 4.5x via hyper-localized promotions on Mercado Libre. In North America, we're holding 12.1% share but gaining traction in eco-friendly variants, where "GreenGuard" fabric softeners grew 22% YoY versus a 2% category decline, aligning with Nielsen's sustainability shopper data showing 40% preference shift. Europe lagged slightly at +110 bps to 10.2%, pressured by regulatory hurdles on phosphates, but our R&D pivot to bio-based surfactants positions us for regulatory tailwinds under the EU Green Deal.  

Snacks & Beverages – 25% of Revenue. This high-velocity category saw us add 80 bps to reach 9.8% global share, navigating health-conscious headwinds better than peers like Mondelez and PepsiCo. Functional snacks led with 190 bps gains in protein bars, where "PeakFuel" bars—fortified with 20g plant-based protein—outperformed Clif Bar by 12% in velocity per IRI scans. North America drove 140 bps to 11.3% share, bolstered by retail media networks (RMNs) on Walmart and Kroger platforms, yielding a 6x media ROI. Asia-Pacific was transformative: +210 bps to 7.9% share, with ready-to-drink (RTD) teas expanding 28% in China via Tmall partnerships, capitalizing on the $15B RTD tea market growing at 10% CAGR. Europe remains a work-in-progress at +40 bps to 8.4%, where sugar taxes bit into carbonated soft drinks; we're offsetting with zero-sugar "VitaSpark" waters, targeting a 100 bps gain in H2 through in-store sampling and velocity-building merchandisers.  

Zooming out regionally: North America (50% of sales) contributed 60% of our share gains, with total share at 13.5% (+160 bps), underscoring our strength in shopper marketing and data analytics via our proprietary Consumer Insights Engine, which optimizes assortment for 85% of ACV households. Emerging markets—Latin America and Asia-Pacific (30% combined)—delivered outsized growth at +240 bps average, reflecting our "glocal" strategy: 70% global brands, 30% tailored locals like our chili-lime snacks for Mexico. Europe (15%) grew more modestly at +100 bps to 11.2%, but we're accelerating with €50M in sustainability capex for recyclable packaging, targeting Unilever-like premiums.  

Key initiatives fueling these trends include: (1) Digital Shelf Leadership: 25% YoY increase in e-comm share-of-voice, with AI-driven personalization boosting conversion 18%; (2) Innovation Pipeline: 12 new SKUs launched this quarter, with 40% hitting 10%+ category share within 6 months; (3) Supply Chain Resilience: Dual-sourcing 60% of raw materials mitigated cocoa and palm oil volatility, preserving 2-3% margins; and (4) Trade Investment Discipline: Promo efficiency at 3.8x ROI, focusing on high-elasticity events like back-to-school.  

Looking forward, we expect continued share accretion of 100-150 bps in FY24, prioritizing premium adjacencies and emerging market velocity. Our category teams are laser-focused on these levers amid a stabilizing macro—U.S. inflation cooling to 3%, China reopening fully.  

As we wrap up our Q3 results, I want to dive deeper into one of our key growth engines: new product launches and our innovation pipeline. In the CPG space, where private label pressures and inflationary headwinds are squeezing margins—think the 4-6% CPI inflation we've seen across staples—innovation isn't just a nice-to-have; it's table stakes for outpacing category growth. Our portfolio delivered 8% organic sales growth this quarter, with new products contributing 12% of that, up from 9% last year. That's ahead of the IRI benchmark for top-quartile CPG innovators, which typically see 7-10% from new items.  

Let me start with our recent launches, which have hit the ground running. In snacks—our $2.5 billion powerhouse segment—we rolled out "VitaCrunch Plant-Powered Bites" in late Q2 across North America. These are high-protein, 100% plant-based crisps using pea protein isolates and upcycled chickpea flour, targeting the $15 billion better-for-you snack occasion. We've achieved 65% ACV distribution in just four months, with Nielsen scan data showing 2.5x category velocity versus established players like PepsiCo's Off the Eaten Path. Early repeat purchase rates are at 28% after 12 weeks—strong, considering the 20% industry average for novel formats. This launch is already pacing for $150 million in full-year incremental revenue, capturing share from legacy extruded snacks amid the 15% CAGR in plant-based snacking per SPINS data.  

Shifting to beverages, our "PureFlow Hydrate" line—functional waters infused with electrolytes from sea minerals and adaptogens like ashwagandha—launched in EMEA and APAC in July. Inspired by the premium hydration boom, akin to Celsius or Prime's explosive growth, we've priced it at a 25% premium to mainstream waters. In the UK and Germany, we've hit 45% ACV in grocery and convenience, driving 18% household penetration in test markets. Sales velocity is 3x that of our core bottled water SKU, with e-commerce—via Amazon and our DTC site—accounting for 35% of volume. Regionally, APAC is the standout: in Australia and Southeast Asia, where heatwave-driven hydration demand spiked 12% YoY, PureFlow has gained 2 points of market share per Kantar, projecting $100 million in FY24 contributions.  

Personal care rounded out the trio with "EcoGlow Renew" shampoos and conditioners, featuring biotech-derived biosurfactants from yeast fermentation—a clean-label alternative to sulfates. Launched in the Americas, this taps the $80 billion global hair care market's shift toward microbiome-friendly formulas, much like L'Oréal's market-leading Seedphyto line. We've secured 55% ACV at mass retailers like Walmart and Target, with 22% trial rates from sampling programs. Notably, sustainability resonates: 40% of buyers cite our 100% PCR packaging—post-consumer recycled PET—as a purchase driver, aligning with Nielsen's finding that 78% of global consumers change habits for eco-friendly products.  

These launches aren't one-offs; they're fueled by our $450 million annual R&D investment—2.8% of sales, in line with P&G and Unilever peers. Our innovation funnel has matured: of 250 concepts ideated last year, 45 advanced to development, 15 to test markets, and 5 commercialized. Success rates improved to 33% from 25% in 2022, thanks to AI-driven consumer insights. We're leveraging tools like our proprietary "InsightAI" platform—built on NLP and computer vision—to analyze 50 million social media mentions and 10,000 shelf-set images quarterly. This cut formulation time by 30% for VitaCrunch, predicting flavor profiles with 85% accuracy.  

Looking ahead to the pipeline, we're accelerating with 12 major launches slated for FY24 and 20 in FY25. Q4 highlights include: Snacks: "FlexFuel Energy Bars" in North America—keto-friendly with mushroom beta-glucans for sustained energy. Pre-launch IRI modeling projects $200 million run-rate, targeting the $6 billion bar category growing at 9% CAGR. Beverages: APAC-exclusive "ZenBrew Kombucha Elixirs" with low-sugar, live probiotics via precision fermentation tech from our partnership with Perfect Day. Aiming for 50% ACV in China and India, where functional beverages are exploding 20% YoY per Euromonitor. Personal Care: EMEA roll of "BarrierBoost Skincare" lotions using ceramide liposomes from lab-grown algae—addressing the post-COVID skin barrier repair trend. We've got co-manufacturing locked in with a European biotech firm, with pilots showing 15% superior moisture retention vs. CeraVe benchmarks.  

Regionally, we're tailoring to local dynamics. In the Americas, premiumization rules: new products average 20% price premiums, offsetting 3% input cost inflation from cocoa and palm oil. EMEA faces regulatory tailwinds like the EU Green Deal, so 70% of our pipeline incorporates circular packaging—think refill pods compatible with Colgate's systems. APAC is volume-driven: we're scaling sachet formats for Indonesia's $10 billion sachet economy, where penetration exceeds 80% in low-income households.  

Strategically, this pipeline positions us for 10-12% organic growth through 2026. We're doubling down on three megatrends: health & wellness (50% of pipeline, mirroring the 25% category shift per Innova Market Insights), sustainability (30%, with Scope 3 emissions down 15% via supplier regen-ag programs), and digital-first (20%, with AR try-on apps boosting DTC conversion 40%). Risks? Supply chain volatility—e.g., stevia shortages—but we've hedged with dual-sourcing and vertical integration in pea protein via our JV with a Canadian grower.  

Competition-wise, we're out-innovating: while Mondelez chases chocolate indulgence, our savory health focus steals share. Against Reckitt's wellness push, our biotech edge gives formulation superiority. Bottom line: innovation drove 300 bps of margin expansion this quarter via higher-velocity SKUs and 15% lower launch costs from modular platforms.  

Good afternoon, everyone. Before I hand it back to Sarah, let me provide some color on our outlook for organic sales growth, which remains our North Star metric as we navigate a dynamic macroeconomic environment. As you know, organic sales growth strips out the noise from FX, M&A, and divestitures, giving you the purest read on our core business momentum—pricing actions, volume/mix dynamics, and distribution gains.  

For the fourth quarter, we're guiding organic sales growth of 3% to 4%. This reflects a sequential moderation from our Q3 print of 4.2%, but still ahead of our long-term algorithm of 3-5%. Breaking it down: Pricing contribution: Expect +2.5% to 3%, down from Q3's 3.8% as inflation eases globally. In North America, we'll hold modest list price increases of 1-2% on select SKUs in our Fabric Care and Household segments—think Tide Pods equivalents and Mr. Clean multi-surfaces—to offset lingering commodity headwinds like palm oil and PET resin, which are stabilizing but up 5% YoY per Bloomberg data. EMEA will see more aggressive pricing at +3.5%, targeting value-pack resets in Beauty & Personal Care amid Eurozone inflation ticking above 2.5%.  

Volume/mix: +0.5% to +1%, driven by market share gains in high-velocity categories. We're leaning into premiumization trends, with 60/40 mix shift toward 'super-premium' tiers—like our relaunched Apex Glow serum line, which posted 12% velocity uplift in test markets, echoing Unilever's Dove Nutrium success. Volumes could face a slight 0.5% headwind from consumer downtrading in Snacks & Beverages, where pantry-loading has normalized post the at-home surge.  

Regionally: North America (55% of sales): 3.5-4.5% organic, fueled by e-commerce acceleration. Amazon ACV now at 98% for our top 20 SKUs, up from 92% last year, with Walmart+ integration driving 15% basket uplift in Health & Wellness. Health-conscious trends are tailwinds—our Apex Pure protein bars are gaining 2 points share vs. Clif and RXBAR, per IRI data. EMEA (20%): 2-3%, tempered by sluggish UK volumes amid cost-of-living pressures. We're countering with targeted promos on Oral Care (e.g., Crest 3D White analogs) and sustainability plays—our recyclable packaging on Persil detergents has boosted loyalty by 8% in Nielsen panels. APAC/LatAm (25%): 4-5%, our growth engine. China rebounding with +6% on Beauty via Tmall Live streams, mirroring P&G's Olay gains. Brazil volumes up on soccer-season hydration packs, though Argentina FX volatility caps pricing.  

For the full fiscal year 2025, we're raising our organic sales growth guidance to 3.5% to 4.5%, from prior 3-4%. This implies a strong Q1 ramp to 4-5%, assuming no recessionary pull-forward.  

Key strategic enablers: Innovation pipeline: 1,200+ new products launching, 40% superior to category averages per SymphonyAI modeling. Highlights include plant-based extensions in our Hellmann's mayo franchise (targeting Beyond Meat adjacencies) and AI-optimized formulations for Skin Health, reducing development cycles by 25%. Distribution expansion: +1.5 points weighted distribution globally, with hyperscaler partnerships like Instacart and Shopee adding 500 bps in digital velocity. We're pruning low-velocity SKUs—rationalized 15% of our 5,000-item portfolio last year, boosting margins by 50 bps. Supply chain resilience: Post-2024 disruptions, our S&OP tech stack (SAP IBP integrated with AI forecasting) has de-risked 80% of our nodes, enabling faster shelf replenishment and 2% volume capture from competitors like Reckitt.  

Risks to watch: Persistent 3-4% food-at-home inflation per USDA could pressure low-income tiers, prompting more trade-down to private label—our IRI share in Mass channels held at 28%, but we're vigilant. Geopolitics in LatAm adds FX noise, though 70% hedged.  

This guidance embeds our disciplined Core EPS growth of 5-7%, funded by $1.2B in productivity savings—supply chain digitization and zero-based budgeting yielding 200 bps gross margin expansion.  

We're positioned to outperform in a 2-3% industry backdrop, per Kantar estimates, by doubling down on consumer-centric innovation and omnichannel execution.  

Good afternoon, everyone. Before we open the line for Q&A, I'd like to dive deep into our gross margin guidance and the key assumptions underpinning it, as this remains a cornerstone of our profitability story in the CPG landscape.  

For the full year 2024, we're reaffirming our gross margin guidance of 51% to 52%, representing approximately 150 basis points of expansion versus our 2023 adjusted gross margin of 49.6%. This builds on the 120 bps sequential improvement we delivered in Q3, where margins hit 51.2%—our strongest quarterly print since pre-pandemic levels. Looking ahead to Q4, we expect margins to land in the 52% to 53% range, driven by a continued unwind of input cost inflation and our structural cost-saving programs.  

Let me unpack the key assumptions and drivers here, starting with the macro tailwinds. Commodity costs, which make up about 40% of our COGS, are tracking favorably. We've seen cocoa prices peak at $11,500 per metric ton in Q3—up 150% YoY due to West African supply shortages from El Niño-induced droughts—but spot prices have since moderated 15% into Q4 as new crop forecasts from Ivory Coast and Ghana stabilize at 1.8 million tons. Similarly, palm oil (critical for our snacks and personal care segments) is down 8% QoQ to around $850/MT, benefiting from Indonesian yield improvements. Sugar and corn derivatives, key for our beverage portfolio akin to what PepsiCo manages in its snacks arm, are flat to down 3% on ample Brazilian and U.S. harvests. Overall, we assume input cost deflation of 2-3% in Q4, versus the 5% inflation headwind we lapped from last year.  

FX remains a modest tailwind. With 55% of our revenues from international markets, a 5% USD strengthening year-to-date has shaved about 20 bps off margins via translation effects, but we bake in a stabilizing EUR at 1.08, BRL at 5.50, and CNY at 7.20 for Q4. No major hedges are rolling off until H1 2025, where we'll layer in forwards at current levels.  

Pricing discipline is our biggest lever, contributing 80 bps to this year's expansion. We've executed 4-6% list price increases across core categories—beauty and household care up 5.5% in EMEA, snacks up 4% in North America—while holding everyday low prices (EDLP) steady to protect volume. Elasticity has held in at -2.5x, better than the -3.5x category average tracked by IRI data, thanks to our premiumization strategy. For context, initiatives like reformulating our 'FreshGlow' skincare line with bio-derived actives have shifted mix +200 bps toward high-margin prestige packs, mirroring L'Oréal's success in the $150B global beauty market.  

Operationally, our 'CPG Efficiency 2.0' program is firing on all cylinders, targeting $450 million in savings for 2024—up from $400 million guided last quarter. This includes: Supply chain optimization: AI-driven demand forecasting via our partnership with Blue Yonder has reduced inventory by 12% to 8.2 weeks of supply, cutting obsolescence 25%. We've consolidated 15 DCs into 10 regionally, yielding 3% logistics savings—think Procter & Gamble's supply chain playbook but accelerated with RPA bots handling 70% of procurement workflows. Manufacturing productivity: Automation upgrades at our top 20 plants (e.g., high-speed pouching lines for snacks) are delivering 5% throughput gains, with OEE now at 88% versus 82% in 2023. Sustainable sourcing—80% RSPO-certified palm oil—avoids $20 million in EU deforestation tariffs starting 2025. Zero-based productivity: Category-specific ZBP reviews have rationalized 300 SKUs, pruning low-margin 'trade-up' items and reallocating to winners like our plant-based 'EverVita' beverages, which grew 25% YoY at 55% margins.  

Regionally, the picture is nuanced: North America (45% of sales): Margins expanding 200 bps to 53%, fueled by 7% pricing in laundry (our Tide-like 'PureClean' brand) and moderating dairy costs. Promo intensity is easing post-back-to-school, with ACV at 75% versus 85% peak. EMEA (25%): 180 bps gain to 50.5%, despite lingering energy costs from the Ukraine conflict. Turkey and UK inflation is abating, but we assume 2% FX drag. APAC/LatAm (30%): Strongest at 250 bps to 49%, with China volumes rebounding 4% on post-COVID normalcy and Brazil pricing up 8% on resilient consumer spending. India remains a margin accelerator via local sourcing of spices, down 10% cost.  

Strategically, we're shaping the portfolio for sustained 53%+ margins long-term. Post our divestiture of low-margin private-label pet food (closed Q2 for $1.2B), 85% of our portfolio now scores 50%+ on our margin heat map. Innovation pipeline—$300M R&D spend—focuses on high-margin adjacencies: functional snacks with protein fortification (targeting 60% margins like Mondelez's Oreo evolutions) and DTC e-comm channels, now 15% of sales at 58% margins versus 48% brick-and-mortar.  

Risks to this guidance? Upside from faster commodity relief could add 50 bps; downside from a cocoa relapse or renewed China lockdowns caps at -75 bps. We're well-hedged with $2B in inventory buffers and flexible contracts covering 70% of 2025 inputs.  

In summary, our gross margin trajectory reflects disciplined execution amid a normalizing CPG environment—input relief, pricing power, and productivity compounding for durable expansion. We're positioned to outperform peers like Colgate-Palmolive or Kimberly-Clark, who guide flat-to-up low-single digits.  

Next, I will turn the call over to Lisa Patel to discuss marketing and brand performance.  

Lisa Patel:  
Thank you, Michael. We saw strong performance in our core brands, particularly in premium segments. Our digital marketing efforts are driving significant engagement, and we are seeing strong results from our Refresh Revolution campaign.  

Good afternoon, everyone. Before I hand over to Sarah for strategic updates, I'd like to dive deep into our marketing campaign effectiveness, a core driver of our 8% YoY top-line growth this quarter. As you know, in the CPG space, marketing isn't just about awareness—it's about delivering measurable shopper activation, household penetration lift, and sustainable ROAS in a fragmented media landscape dominated by retail media networks like Amazon DSP and Kroger Precision Marketing.  

Let me start with the big picture. Our absolute A&M spend came in at $1.2 billion for the first half of the year, up 4% YoY, representing 12.5% of net sales—right in line with peers like Procter & Gamble and Unilever, who are hovering around 11-13%. But what's impressive is the efficiency: our blended ROAS across all channels hit 4.8x, a 15% improvement from H1 2023's 4.2x. This was fueled by a disciplined shift in mix—digital and performance marketing now account for 48% of our budget, up from 35% last year, while traditional TV and OOH dipped to 22%. We're leveraging advanced Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) via our partnership with Nielsen and Black Book, which attributes 72% of our sales lift directly to paid media, with the rest from organic brand equity and pricing elasticity.  

Breaking it down by key campaigns, our flagship 'Refresh Revolution' platform for our core beverage portfolio—think FrostPeak sodas and PureVita waters—delivered standout results. Launched in Q1 across 15 markets, it featured user-generated content (UGC) challenges on TikTok and Instagram Reels, inspired by Coca-Cola's 'Share a Coke' personalization but supercharged with AI-driven dynamic creative optimization (DCO). We achieved 2.5 billion impressions, a 28% YoY increase in GRPs, and a staggering 7.2x ROAS. Nielsen IRI data shows a 14% dollar sales lift in measured channels, with household penetration (HHP) jumping 9 points to 42% in the U.S. East and Midwest. Critically, our customer acquisition cost (CAC) for new FrostPeak trialists dropped 22% to $4.50, thanks to lookalike modeling on first-party data from our Apex Rewards loyalty app, which now boasts 18 million active users.  

Regionally, performance varied but trended positive. In North America, which drove 55% of our A&M ROI, the campaign crushed it with a 6.5x ROAS amid softening category volumes—U.S. carbonated soft drinks saw flat IRI growth ex-Apex, per Circana reports. We partnered with Walmart Connect and Target Roundel for shopper marketing, targeting high-propensity households with 15-second video ads on connected TV (CTV), yielding a 18% uplift in ACV (All Commodity Volume) distribution. Europe was more challenged: EMEA ROAS at 3.9x, pressured by inflation-weary consumers and regulatory scrutiny on HFSS (high fat, salt, sugar) advertising. Here, our pivot to sustainability messaging—'Refresh Sustainably' with recyclable packaging calls-to-action—boosted brand favorability 11 points per YouGov tracking, converting to a 7% sales lift in the UK and Germany despite a 2% category decline.  

APAC shone bright at 5.8x ROAS, led by India and China. In India, our FrostPeak Diwali tie-in with local influencers like Bhuvan Bam generated 450 million views, driving 22% volume growth and expanding our market share from 14% to 16.5% in non-cola RTD beverages, edging out PepsiCo's Tropicana. China faced headwinds from zero-COVID hangover and KOL (Key Opinion Leader) saturation, but our Douyin (TikTok China) shoppable lives—integrated with Tmall's clean room tech—achieved a 12:1 ROAS on direct-to-consumer sales, with repeat purchase rates up 30%. LatAm rounded out at 4.2x, where Brazil's Carnival activations via Globo TV and Shopee Ads lifted PureVita HHP by 13 points in urban markets.  

On the technical front, we're ahead of the curve with several initiatives. First, our in-house AI platform, Apex Pulse, uses machine learning for multi-touch attribution, reducing cookie dependency by 65% through contextual signals and first-party CRM data. We've invested $50 million in probabilistic modeling with The Trade Desk, enabling cross-device stitching that improved digital incrementality by 24%. Second, retail media is now 25% of our spend—double YoY—with closed-loop reporting from Criteo and CitrusAd showing 8x ROAS on average. We're also piloting privacy-safe data clean rooms with Instacart and DoorDash to measure offsite lift on on-site conversions. These tools helped us cut waste: ad frequency capped at 5.2 exposures per user, down from 7.1, boosting CPM efficiency 17%.  

Strategically, these results affirm our 'Precision Growth' playbook: prioritizing performance over reach in a high-interest-rate environment where CPG velocity is king. We're learning that emotional storytelling—à la Dove's Real Beauty—still drives long-term brand health (up 6 points on our BrandZ index), but it must pair with bottom-funnel activation. Key insight: sustainability claims now yield 2.2x higher engagement among Gen Z, per our Kantar Worldpanel analysis, so we're allocating 15% of next quarter's budget to eco-focused creator partnerships.  

Looking forward, we expect Q3 ROAS to hold at 4.7x-5.0x, supported by back-to-school activations and holiday pre-loading. We'll ramp digital to 52% of spend, targeting $1.5 billion in attributable sales lift for FY24. Risks include potential iOS privacy changes eroding 10-15% of mobile attribution, but our first-party stack mitigates that.
